bga_name: Roll Through the Ages: The Bronze Age
rules_text:
Rules summary Table 1 – Dice Results Result Collect Effect 3 Food 3 Food Add 3 food to your peg board. 1 Good 1 Good Worth 1 good. Add multiple goods to separate rows, e.g., 1 = 1 wood; 2 = 1 wood + 1 stone; 3 = 1 wood + 1 stone + 1 pottery, and so on. 2 Goods and 1 Skull 2 Goods and 1 Skull Worth 2 goods and 1 skull. After rolling all dice, if a player has more than 1 skull showing, a disaster will occur. Skulls do not accumulate from round to round. 3 Workers 3 Workers Check off 3 boxes in cities and/or monuments of your choice. 2 Food or 2 Workers 2 Food or 2 Workers Feed 2 cities or check off 2 boxes to build cities and/or monuments. 7 Coins 7 Coins Worth 7 coins toward a development. Coins cannot be saved from round to round. Table 2 – Disaster Results Cause Result Effect Affected By No Food Famine Lose 1 point for each city Food (1 food needed per city). 1 Skull None No effect Not applicable 2 Skulls Drought Lose 2 points If you have Irrigation, you are unaffected 3 Skulls Pestilence Your opponents lose 3 points Opponents with Medicine are unaffected 4 Skulls Invasion Lose 4 points If you have completed the Great Wall monument, you are unaffected 5+ Skulls Revolt Lose all your goods (including those just collected) If you have Religion, instead of losing all of your goods, your opponents lose all of their goods. Opponents with Religion are unaffected.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Get more cities. (= more dice) Buy Quarry, camp stone until you hit Empire. Between those, Medicine. Now Masons/Monument until somebody ends it. Why do anything else?

[Rating: 1/10] easily one of the worst games I have ever played.  No player interaction, minuscule strategy.  Yahtzee is a much better game in that it at least asks you to do some math in your head.

[Rating: 1/10] Inherently broken. The person who rolls the most workers earlier on in the game has far to great of an advantage. Workers = more dice = better odds = purchase of developments and building of monuments quicker = massive advantage = run away leader = broken game.

[Rating: 1/10] Rips off Through the Ages - this is nothing like it and horrible.  BGG also contains incorrect info about this game, beware.

[Rating: 2/10] The less sophisticated, shorter version of its bigger brother. While I haven't played the longer version, this dice-rolling version is mildly interesting. It's Yahtzee on steroids, I suppose. Roll some dice to get resources and workers, to turn them into developments and monuments. Developments help you fend off disasters which can occur with rolling the dice. Seems straightforward, but the 3P game ended far too quickly. Could it be a good filler? I don't know--I'm now intrigued to play its bigger brother soon.  Update (08/17/10): I am convinced that I should stay away from all "roll this and 

[Rating: 2/10] A roll and write from times before roll and write became popular.   Good things: - a bit more involved R%W because it's engine building and a thematic one at that.   Mediocre things: - late bronze age variant is better - fell like director's cut. Engines run a bit longer, some interaction if memory serves.   Ugly things: - I dislike wooden components. Would prefer plastic dice and cardboard boards.   Conclusion: - meh. traded away. don't miss.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't like DICE. FUCKIN' down time! TOOOOOOOOOOOO much LOOOONG!! I don't wanna play anymore.

[Rating: 2/10] This is a fairly bad dice-version of a very good game. Risk Express is much better because it doesn't pretend to be complicated.

[Rating: 2/10] "Yahtzee" or "Ship, Captain, Crew" with record-keeping.  What an awful game.  I suppose if you were drunk, and tripping on 'shrooms, and developmentally challenged to begin with, it could be an interesting way to kill some time in a completely mindless way.  I mean, sure, it's okay if you're into games like "Yahtzee" and "Monopoly", but then:  why are you here (on BGG, not Earth)?  People who say "It's like Civ, but it plays in 20 minutes!" are stupid.  It's nothing at all like Civ.  IT'S YAHTZEE.  You just. roll. dice.   Then roll again.  Then roll again.  Move pegs.  Check boxes.  Roll dice.

[Rating: 2/10] Whomever rolls the most workers early wins. The second game I did not roll any workers for the first 2/3 of the game. I came in last. The guy who rolled the most early workers came in first. The guy who rolled the second most early workers came in second. The guy who rolled the third most came in second.  Extremely unlikely I will play it again.
